title: The scaffold ships node-pg-migrate and the generated app migrates green
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-8f86e10504c74e248ccfa6f427b41a15 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF.

ARCHITECT DECISION on the question the parent left open ("architect picks drizzle-kit or node-pg-migrate; pinned"): NODE-PG-MIGRATE. Reasons, so it is not re-litigated: (1) drizzle-kit implies adopting DRIZZLE ORM as the generated product's data layer - a far larger commitment that constrains how every future node writes schema and query code, for a row whose subject is only migrations; (2) this feature needs first-class REVERT (`db:migrate:down`, and `deployment.migrate_down` reverting the last batch), and node-pg-migrate has an explicit up/down per migration while SQL-diff generators handle down poorly; (3) plain migration files are easier for a CODING SEAT to author correctly than a schema file plus generated diffs, and seats are who will write them; (4) it is PostgreSQL-specific, which matches the controlled profile exactly. PIN THE VERSION.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the scaffold profile's migration surface - the pinned tool, `pnpm db:migrate` and `pnpm db:migrate:down` scripts, a `migrations/` directory with an initial migration - and the proof that the generated app actually migrates against a real disposable PostgreSQL. No verifier leg, no deploy, no UI.

COORDINATION, NOT A DEPENDENCY: the scaffold generator belongs to task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0 (under the repository-bootstrapping parent), whose golden test pins the generated tree under a PROFILE VERSION constant. This row CHANGES that tree, so it is a profile version BUMP, not an edit in place, and that row's golden test moves with it. Check which of the two landed first and coordinate - do not fork a second scaffold.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): no migration tooling anywhere. `grep -rn 'db:migrate|MIGRATION_' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` finds only unrelated scheduler fairness constants (fairness-cap-revision.ts:53, fairness-aging.ts:110). The gap is real.
definitionOfDone: The scaffold profile ships node-pg-migrate at a PINNED version, with `pnpm db:migrate` and `pnpm db:migrate:down` scripts and a `migrations/` directory containing an initial migration. The scaffold golden test (task-4a0f7064's) is updated as a PROFILE VERSION BUMP rather than an edit in place, so a product's starting tree stays identifiable by its version.

THE GENERATED APP ACTUALLY MIGRATES: a test starts a disposable PostgreSQL, runs the generated app's `pnpm db:migrate` against it, and asserts the schema exists afterwards (assert a table from the initial migration is present, not merely that the command exited 0 - a migration tool with nothing to do also exits 0). Quote the CHILD run's output, labelled as the generated product's, never conflated with moe-next's own gates.

`pnpm db:migrate:down` REVERTS it: run down and assert the table is gone. This is the arm that makes `deployment.migrate_down` possible later, and the reason node-pg-migrate was chosen over a diff generator - if down does not work cleanly here, say so now rather than after the deploy path depends on it.

MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING is defined with its layer for a workspace that declares no `db:migrate` script (the code is raised by children 2 and 3 - define it here and say where it is exercised rather than manufacturing a call site).

Determinism holds: the migration filenames and the initial migration's bytes are stable across two generations, since node-pg-migrate names files by timestamp by default and a timestamped filename would break the scaffold golden test. State how you pinned it.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NODE-PG-MIGRATE, PINNED. The decision and its reasons are in the description; do not substitute drizzle-kit, and do not pull in an ORM - this row adds migrations, not a data layer.
A CHANGE TO THE SCAFFOLD IS A PROFILE VERSION BUMP, coordinated with task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0's golden test. Never fork a second scaffold generator.
TIMESTAMPED MIGRATION FILENAMES BREAK DETERMINISM. node-pg-migrate names by timestamp by default and the scaffold golden test requires byte-identical trees - pin it and say how.
PROVE UP AND DOWN AGAINST A REAL POSTGRES. `exit 0` is not proof: a tool with nothing to do also exits 0.
NO VERIFIER LEG, NO DEPLOY, NO UI: those are children 2 and 3.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE, AND SETTLE THE VERSION-BUMP CONSEQUENCE THE ROW DOES NOT MENTION. NO EDITS. (a) THE SCAFFOLD IS ALREADY LANDED: task-4a0f7064 is DONE and lives at `apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/` - generator.ts (136), root-templates.ts (215), package-templates.ts (250), generator.test.ts (248), build.test.ts (173), plus `.js` bridges and an `assets/` dir. So the row's "check which of the two landed first and coordinate" is settled: it landed, you extend it, and `dependsOn` needs nothing. (b) THE BUMP RETIRES THE OLD VERSION, AND THAT MUST BE A DECISION. `isKnownProfileVersion` (generator.ts:74) is `return value === CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` - a STRICT SINGLE-VALUE equality against `"controlled-1"` (:26). Bump to `controlled-2` and every request naming `controlled-1` refuses `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN`. I measured whether that strands anything: `git grep -n 'CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION|profileVersion' -- apps/daemon/src` OUTSIDE that directory returns NOTHING - no record persists a profile version, and the bootstrap command that would write one (task-facff1d1) is still PLANNING. So retiring `controlled-1` strands nothing TODAY. Decide deliberately between retiring it (one known version, one template set) and admitting both (a Set, and TWO template sets to maintain forever), state which and why in the step note, and re-run that grep first in case the bootstrap row landed meanwhile - if a record now stores `controlled-1`, retiring it breaks reading that record and the answer changes. (c) READ THE GOLDEN TEST'S FOUR COUPLED ARMS before touching a template, because three of them move with this change: `manifestOf` vs `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` (:137-152, a `path  sha256` list); the byte pins for package.json / docker-compose.yml / the CI workflow (:155-160); byte-identity across two generations (:163-167); and `differing == ["README.md", "package.json"]` between two products (:170-182). THAT LAST ONE IS A TRAP: it asserts the product NAME reaches exactly two files, so if your migration or its config embeds the product name, that arm reds and the fix is to keep the name OUT of the migration files, not to widen the list. (d) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (e) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/repository/` and note peer dirt; never revert it.

THE SCAFFOLD CHANGE, AS A VERSION BUMP. Edit the templates under `apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/`, not a fork (rail 2). (1) Bump `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` at generator.ts:26 per the step-1 decision. (2) `controlled-profile-package-templates.ts` / `root-templates.ts`: add node-pg-migrate to the generated package.json at a PINNED EXACT version, plus `db:migrate` and `db:migrate:down` scripts. root-templates.ts:10-12 states the rule you are following - "VERSION PINS are what make `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` hold in the generated product... Editing any of them is a profile VERSION BUMP plus a LOCKFILE RE-MINT, not an edit in place." (3) THE LOCKFILE IS THE EASY MISS AND IT BREAKS THE GENERATED PRODUCT, NOT THIS REPO. The scaffold emits a committed `pnpm-lock.yaml` (generator.ts:129 `["pnpm-lock.yaml", lockfileBytes()]`), and both the generated README (:114) and its CI workflow (:169) run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. A package.json gaining a dependency whose lockfile did not is a FROZEN-LOCKFILE FAILURE in every product this profile ever generates - and moe-next's own gates would stay green while it happened. Re-mint the lockfile bytes and say how you produced them. (4) A `migrations/` directory with ONE initial migration. DoD-5 IS EASIER THAN IT LOOKS AND THE PLAN SAYS SO: node-pg-migrate timestamps filenames when ITS CLI creates a migration, but the scaffold WRITES THIS FILE ITSELF as a template, so its name is whatever you hardcode and determinism is free. What you must decide is what happens LATER, when a coding seat runs the tool to author migration two - state in the step note whether you pinned a non-timestamp naming convention in the tool's config or accepted timestamps for seat-authored files (the golden test only pins the SCAFFOLD's tree, so the second is defensible). Do not invent a problem the generator does not have, and do not leave the seat's case unanswered. (5) Keep the PRODUCT NAME out of every file you add - see step 1(c).

THE GOLDEN TEST MOVES WITH THE BUMP. `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts` (248 lines). Update `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` for the new paths and hashes, and the byte pins for package.json (the new dependency and scripts) - taking every hash from the PRINTED expected-vs-received of a failing run, never from arithmetic or a hand-computed digest. Re-assert, do not weaken: byte-identity across two generations must still hold, and `differing` between two products must still be exactly `["README.md", "package.json"]` - if that arm reds, the product name leaked into a migration file and the fix is in step 2, not here. ADD ONE ARM THIS ROW OWES THE NEXT ROW: assert the generated package.json declares BOTH `db:migrate` and `db:migrate:down`, by name. Children 2 and 3 raise `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` for a workspace that declares no `db:migrate` script, so the scaffold's promise that it always does is the thing they build on, and it deserves an assertion that is not a byte pin - a byte pin reds for any package.json change, which tells the next reader nothing about WHICH promise broke. DoD-4: define `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` with its layer, reusing an ALREADY-ROSTERED layer literal (a new `*_LAYER` constant demands a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own). The code is RAISED by children 2 and 3 - define it here, and say in the completion record where it is exercised rather than manufacturing a call site to reach it.

THE REAL-POSTGRES PROOF, ON THE PRECEDENT THAT ALREADY EXISTS. DoD-2 and DoD-3 need a disposable PostgreSQL, and `controlled-profile-build.test.ts` (173 lines) has already solved this exact problem for the build proof - READ ITS HEADER FIRST, it is the design: the expensive arm is OPT-IN behind `MOE_SCAFFOLD_BUILD=1` because unconditionally it "would execute inside `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, the gate every row on this board runs, and would red on any offline host - making every later gate on the board inadmissible". A migration arm needs a real database and is strictly worse on that axis, so gate it the same way, and follow the two things that stop an opt-in becoming a decoration: an ALWAYS-ON arm asserting precisely the preconditions whose absence would make the expensive arm vacuous (here: that the scripts and the migrations directory exist in the generated tree, so an opt-in run has something to run), and a completion record quoting the expensive arm's OWN output with a ZERO SKIPPED count from a run with the flag set. Copy its leg discipline verbatim: "Four SEPARATE foreground legs. Never an `&&` chain (reports only the last status) or a pipe." UP AND DOWN, BOTH ASSERTED ON THE SCHEMA (DoD-2, DoD-3): run `db:migrate` and assert a TABLE FROM THE INITIAL MIGRATION IS PRESENT - `exit 0` is not proof, because a migration tool with nothing to do also exits 0 - then run `db:migrate:down` and assert the table is GONE. The down arm is the one that makes `deployment.migrate_down` possible later and is the whole reason node-pg-migrate was chosen over a diff generator; if down does not revert cleanly, SAY SO NOW rather than after the deploy path depends on it. EPIC RAIL 4 APPLIES TO THE DATABASE ITSELF: the container, its volume and any temp directory are released on EVERY exit path INCLUDING THE THROWING ONE - teardown in a `finally`, never after the assertions. A leaked postgres container makes every later gate on this board inadmissible. Label the child run's output as the GENERATED PRODUCT's, never conflated with moe-next's own gates.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. MIXED: the migrate test is NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is BLIND to it - SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id), proved in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The four template and test files are TRACKED and take an empty `git diff`. Say which proof applies to which path. THREE DRILLS: (i) THE LOCKFILE DRILL, and the one that protects the generated product rather than this repo - revert the lockfile bytes while keeping the new dependency in package.json, then run the opt-in build arm and confirm `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` FAILS in the child. Quote it. That is the failure that would otherwise ship silently in every product this profile generates while moe-next's own gates stayed green. (ii) Make the initial migration a no-op (create nothing) and confirm the DoD-2 arm reds - if it stays green it was asserting `exit 0`, which a tool with nothing to do also returns. (iii) Make `db:migrate:down` a no-op and confirm the DoD-3 arm reds naming the table that should have been dropped. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence here - vitest.config.ts:32 has no `apps/**`. AND SEPARATELY, the opt-in arms with their flags set, quoted with a ZERO SKIPPED count - an opt-in arm nobody ran is not evidence, and the build test's header says so in those words. Keep the generated product's child output clearly labelled as the child's. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: does the migration or its config embed the product name (the `differing` arm); does `db:migrate:down` revert ONE migration or ALL of them, and is that what `deployment.migrate_down` will want (children 2 and 3 build on this answer - state it); what happens when `db:migrate` runs twice; a migration directory the tool cannot read; the postgres container left alive on a throwing path; whether the CI workflow arm at generator.test.ts:194 should now gate migrations too, and if you decided not to, why. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the profile version you bumped to and whether the old one is RETIRED or still admitted, with the grep that shows what it strands; the pinned node-pg-migrate version and how you re-minted the lockfile; the seat-authored-migration naming decision from step 2(4); the up and down arms' own output with a zero skipped count, labelled as the generated product's; drill (i) verbatim; and where `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` is exercised, since it is defined here and raised by children 2 and 3.

comments.content:
THE LOCKFILE IS THIS ROW'S REAL HAZARD AND THE DoD DOES NOT MENTION IT. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 5 files, 1 new.

Tool decision left as-is — rail 1 settles it and the four reasons hold, particularly first-class per-migration down, which is what `deployment.migrate_down` needs later.

## The lockfile

The scaffold emits a **committed** `pnpm-lock.yaml` (generator.ts:129), and both the generated README (root-templates.ts:114) and its CI workflow (:169) run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. That file's own header states the rule: *"VERSION PINS are what make `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` hold in the generated product… Editing any of them is a profile VERSION BUMP plus a lockfile re-mint, not an edit in place."*

So a package.json gaining node-pg-migrate whose lockfile did not is a **frozen-lockfile failure in every product this profile ever generates** — while moe-next's own gates stay green throughout. Drill (i) reverts the lockfile bytes and requires the child install to fail.

## The bump retires `controlled-1` by construction

`isKnownProfileVersion` (generator.ts:74) is `value === CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` — a strict single-value equality. Bump to `controlled-2` and every `controlled-1` request refuses `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN`.

I measured what that strands: `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION`/`profileVersion` appear **nowhere** outside `controlled-profile/`, nothing persists a version, and the bootstrap command that would write one (task-facff1d1) is still PLANNING. So retiring strands nothing *today* — but it is a decision to state, not to stumble into, and the plan makes the worker re-run that grep in case the bootstrap row landed meanwhile.

## DoD-5 is easier than it reads — don't over-build it

node-pg-migrate timestamps filenames when **its CLI** creates one. The scaffold **writes the initial migration itself** as a template, so its name is hardcoded and determinism is free. The real question is what a coding seat does authoring migration two — and the golden test only pins the scaffold's tree, so accepting timestamps there is defensible. The plan asks for that decision rather than a ritual defence against a problem the generator does not have.

## The expensive proof already has a precedent that solves its hardest problem

`controlled-profile-build.test.ts` gates its build arm behind `MOE_SCAFFOLD_BUILD=1` because unconditionally it *"would execute inside `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, the gate every row on this board runs, and would red on any offline host — making every later gate on the board inadmissible."* A migration arm needs a live database and is strictly worse on that axis.

Its header also documents the two things that stop an opt-in becoming a decoration, both carried into step 4: an **always-on** arm asserting the preconditions whose absence would make the expensive arm vacuous, and a completion record quoting the expensive arm's own output with a **zero skipped** count.

## One tripwire in the golden test

`differing == ["README.md", "package.json"]` (generator.test.ts:170-182) asserts the product name reaches exactly two files. If the migration or its config embeds the product name, that arm reds — and the fix is to keep the name **out of the migration files**, not to widen the expected list.

Two contracts children 2 and 3 will build on, so state both: whether `db:migrate:down` reverts **one** migration or **all**, and where `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` is exercised given it is defined here and raised there.
